newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady but asking prices rise.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady but asking prices rise.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges got off to a slow start of the week on Monday, trading at steady numbers with high asking prices said to be stifling deals, traders said.

High sulphur fuel oil barges traded twice at $87 a tonne fob ARA, unchanged from Friday. The deals were done at the midpoint of early talk, $86.50 and $87.50, but mid-day talk widened to the $85/$86 region for buyers and $87/$88 for sellers.
"The prices (asked) are so high, so if you don't need a cargo you don't buy," one trader said.
A second trader said: "There's a lot of bunker demand, but the prices I am offering are too high."
No deals were reported early in the day in low sulphur barges but there was unconfirmed talk of a deal done on Friday at $95 fob Rotterdam, or $0.50 a tonne higher than two barge trades last week.
The fate of two physical high sulphur cargoes of bunker grade material offered late last week at $79 and $81 was not immediately known, but buying interest was very thin then.
